# MM-P3-L1-IH03 - Maintenance manual - Hot Forge induction billet heater #3

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-IH03

Scope
- This manual provides maintenance tasks, safe work rationale, and acceptance criteria for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03).  
- Applies to preventive and corrective maintenance activities necessary to ensure reliable heating to process setpoints and safe handling of induction coil and cooling systems.  
- Refer to SB-1044, SB-1047, SOP-P3-L1-05 for wiring diagrams, safety barriers, and operational procedures.

Background and purpose
- EQ-P3-L1-IH03 is an induction billet heater used to raise billets to process temperature prior to forging. Proper coil condition and cooling are critical to maintain heat transfer efficiency and asset life.  
- The target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 1260 °C. Maintaining uniform coil impedance and adequate cooling prevents overheating of the coil and nearby components, reduces unplanned downtime, and ensures part quality.

Tools and consumables
- Insulation-resistant gloves and arc-rated face shield per site PPE protocol (see SOP-P3-L1-05).  
- Hand tools for coil clamp adjustment and fastener torqueing (match OEM tool list in SB-1044).  
- Infrared pyrometer or thermocouple reader calibrated to site standard (refer SB-1047 for calibration certificate location).  
- Flow meter portable test rig compatible with induction coil cooling lines.  
- Non-contact vibration scanner for detecting loose coil assemblies.  
- Cooling system test fluid and hose fittings as specified in SB-1044.  
- Tagout/lockout kit consistent with SOP-P3-L1-05.

Procedure
Preparation and safety
- Verify permit and lockout/tagout per SOP-P3-L1-05. Confirm isolations: electrical supply to induction inverter and cooling pump circuits isolated and verified.  
- Inspect PPE and ensure all personnel in the work area are briefed on hazards associated with high temperature, stored energy in capacitors, and pressurized cooling circuits.  
- Gather records: most recent coil impedance baseline and cooling system test log (see records to keep).

Visual and electrical inspection
- With system deenergized and capacitors discharged per SB-1044, inspect coil windings for cracked insulation, hot spots, or evidence of arcing. Remove scale and debris from coil exterior using nonconductive tools. Rationale: physical damage increases localized heating and impedance variance.  
- Inspect coil clamping hardware for looseness; verify mounting studs are secure. Rationale: vibration-driven loosening can change coil geometry and reduce heating uniformity.

Cooling system verification
- Restore cooling system power while maintaining induction inverter locked out to perform cooling checks. Activate cooling pumps and verify flow using the portable flow meter. The coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min. Rationale: insufficient flow reduces heat removal capability and can lead to coil failure.  
- Inspect inlet and outlet lines for leaks, kinks, or deposits. Flush and strain cooling lines if evidence of contamination is found. Note: maintain containment and disposal records per SB-1047.

Electrical continuity and impedance
- With inverter still locked out and safety permits in place, measure coil impedance and compare to baseline documented in the coil condition record. Rationale: impedance drift indicates insulation breakdown, shorted turns, or changes in coil geometry. If deviation from baseline exceeds limits defined in SB-1044, escalate for coil repair or replacement.

Operational functional test
- Return system to normal configuration per SOP-P3-L1-05. Energize induction inverter and perform a low-power heat cycle using operator controls with test billet or equivalent thermal load. Monitor temperature rise with calibrated pyrometer to verify expected heating profile toward the target. Use thermal imaging to verify uniformity across the billet surface. Rationale: small functional tests confirm combined electrical and fluid system health without stressing components.

Examples and troubleshooting
- Example: If flow is measured below the specified 65 L/min, first inspect for closed valves or blocked strainers. If strainers contain debris, clean and retest. If pump output remains low, tag out and initiate pump maintenance as per SB-1044.  
- Example: If measured impedance has increased since baseline, check for loose connections and retighten per torque values in SB-1044, then remeasure. If impedance remains high, schedule coil rewinding or replacement per SB-1044.

Records to keep
- Coil condition inspection report (include photos and measured impedance values).  
- Cooling flow verification log with measured flow and corrective actions. Include the measured coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min entry where applicable.  
- Functional test report with pyrometer readings showing approach toward the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 1260 °C, thermal images, and operator sign-off.  
- Lockout/tagout permit and personnel safety brief record per SOP-P3-L1-05.  
- Any parts replaced, referencing SB-1044 for part identification and SB-1047 for calibration and certification documentation.

Acceptance criteria
- Coil mechanical inspection shows no cracked insulation, no loose mountings, and no signs of arcing.  
- Measured coil impedance falls within the acceptable range documented in SB-1044 compared to baseline.  
- Cooling system achieves at or above the coil cooling water flow minimum for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 65 L/min with no leakage.  
- Operational test demonstrates heating behavior consistent with previous performance and shows control system achieving or trending toward the target billet temperature for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P3-L1-IH03) is 1260 °C.  
- All maintenance actions are recorded, and documentation uploaded to the equipment history file with references to SB-1044, SB-1047, SOP-P3-L1-05.

Notes and escalation
- If any acceptance criterion is not met, cease operation and raise a maintenance work order as per SOP-P3-L1-05. Include all records listed above and notify process engineering and shift supervision.  
- For questions about coil repair scope or inverter interface, consult SB-1044 and SB-1047 prior to performing nonstandard repairs.
